books.section: The Rise of the Service Sector
Prosperity and a New World Order (1988–2000)

stem: What does the photograph most directly show?

options.text: A steel mill running at full capacity
options.misconception: No workers or machinery are in sight.

options.text: A steel mill abandoned after its work moved away

options.misconception: A mill under construction would have workers and new materials, not weeds and an empty yard.

options.text: A steel mill converted into a shopping mall
options.misconception: Nothing in the photograph shows shops or shoppers; it shows an empty mill.

rationales.A: No workers or machinery are in sight.
rationales.B: The photograph shows an empty mill with weeds in the yard and no workers — a mill whose work has gone.
rationales.C: A mill under construction would have workers and new materials, not weeds and an empty yard.
rationales.D: Nothing in the photograph shows shops or shoppers; it shows an empty mill.
rationales.general:
1. Look at what is actually there: an empty mill, weeds in the yard, and nobody at work.
2. A working mill would show workers and machinery.
3. A building site would show builders and new materials.
4. What is left is an empty shell — the work has moved away.
Remember: describe what you see before you explain it.
